title: Sentiment Analysis
description: Analyze the sentiment of any text using machine learning! The model classifies text as Positive, Negative, or Neutral with confidence scores.

ui.placeholder:

howItWorks.title: How it works:
howItWorks.bullet1: The model uses TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency) to convert text to numbers
howItWorks.bullet2: A Logistic Regression classifier predicts sentiment based on word patterns
howItWorks.bullet3: Trained on 45 example sentences (15 positive, 15 negative, 15 neutral)
howItWorks.bullet4: Shows confidence scores for all three sentiment categories
howItWorks.bullet5: All processing happens in your browser using PyScript!

activeLearning.title: 💡 Active Learning
activeLearning.description: After each prediction, you can provide feedback:
activeLearning.feedbackYes: Click YES if correct → Reinforces the model
activeLearning.feedbackNo: Click NO if wrong → Correct it and retrain with the right label
activeLearning.conclusion: The model learns from your feedback and improves over time!

architecture.title: 🏗️ Architecture
architecture.description: This example demonstrates proper separation of concerns:
architecture.python: Python - Pure ML logic, no HTML. Uses to_js() to convert Python dicts to JavaScript objects before calling window callbacks.
architecture.controller: Controller - Business logic layer. Receives plain JS objects and delegates to UIHandler.
architecture.svelte: Svelte UIHandler - Pure UI rendering with reactive state. Updates UI based on plain objects.
architecture.keyLesson: Key lesson: Python dicts must be explicitly converted using to_js(dict, dict_converter=Object.fromEntries) to work properly with JavaScript.

note.title: 📝 Note
note.description: This is a simple demonstration model. For production use, you'd want to train on a much larger dataset (thousands of examples) for better accuracy and generalization.
